analysis: Integration pass over units 52-56 plus replayed source. The PR mechanically rewrites Foundation Date `>=`/`<=` comparisons as `timeIntervalSince(_:) >= 0` or `<= 0`. The replayed changelog and docs say the cause is the SDK 27.2 back-deployed weak imports, which pre-release macOS 27.2 builds lack, so the provider crashes in a loop. The rewritten sites are ClusterService.swift (510, 646, 909, 1044, 1126, 1582), ClusterPairCommands.swift (119, 276), Schedule.swift (189, 196), ScheduleIntervals.swift (23), DesktopAccountEarnings.swift, and EnrollmentKeyLifecycle.swift mayGenerateKey, in the replay. Thresholds are unchanged. `Date.distantPast` yields a large finite positive interval, so the semantics are preserved. The App Attest key-generation budget check keeps its fail-closed `guard` (nil returns false), so there is no TB-011 or T-053/T-057 weakening. The new scripts/check-date-comparisons.py and scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py, with their tests, are build-time tools. The binary checker uses list-argument subprocess calls (nm, otool, xcrun) with no shell. It fails closed on missing binaries. The source lint is heuristic and documents that it can miss comparisons. The release action step is gated on lane == 'release', uses env vars quoted in bash, and runs against built binaries. The workflow path filters add the script, so changes to it trigger release builds. The ci.yml step adds the tests. No change touches authorization, attestation, encryption, keys, the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), the prefix cache (T-041), the add-on hold socket (TB-012), the fan helper, or the installer (TB-013). The security benefit is availability: it prevents a crash loop. Limits: the replay is incomplete (186 units omitted), and the patch excerpt for several ClusterService hunks was truncated, so I assume they are equivalent mechanical rewrites. Whether other Date `>=`/`<=` uses were missed is covered by the binary check, but its CI invocation and enforcement on the release artifacts were not fully visible. These are not security regressions.
